exposure: Excessive gestational weight gain (GWG) during the week prior to delivery
cohort: The study included 94 preeclamptic women and 188 healthy control women, all with singleton pregnancies and delivering at or after 22 gestational weeks.
finding: Excessive gestational weight gain during the week prior to delivery was significantly higher in preeclamptic women and was associated with a higher risk of maternal life-threatening complications, including pulmonary edema, hypoproteinemia, proteinuria, and renal dysfunction.
cross-section timing: During the week prior to delivery
